what: The rooms seen through the shop windows of Quay Street (item 2a, 1 October 2026; Jafar: "fake interiors in the shop windows by interior mapping, as games do it"; method: production/research/shop-window-interiors/NOTE.md). Each shop's room is built and rendered by tools/art-recipes/shop-room.py as one perspective picture from in front of its window, per lighting state, and the game shows it on the bay's interior card with depth (the interior material). Street metres: x along the street, z back from the pavement, heights above the road crown. One complete shop first (the pawnbroker); the rest only after Jafar has seen it in the game (CLAUDE.md: nothing is multiplied before one sample is approved).

states.day: the shop open by day: its tubes on, daylight through the front
states.night_lit: open after dark or a lit window display: tubes on, no daylight
states.night_dark: shut at night: only the street's sodium spill through the front and a faint back light

camera: on the room's centre line, d in front of the front plane, framing the front rectangle W x H exactly (horizontal field 2 atan(W / 2d)); a room point (x, y, z), z behind the front plane, lands at u = 0.5 + (x / W) d / (d + z), v = 0.5 + (y / H) d / (d + z)
never: no people (the town is simulated: a painted figure reads as a witness), no real brands, no alcohol, no gambling (no pools coupons), no children

shops.trade: minicab office (Mickey's): the public side with a vinyl bench under the fares, the licence and the accounts notice; the booking counter across with the book of every fare, two phones, an ashtray, the dockets on their spike; the staff side with the radio set, its desk microphone and the loudspeaker, Mickey's swivel chair empty behind them, the district map and the drivers' board; the door to Sheila's back room ajar; the number in gilt on the glass. Laid out from production/specs/mickeys-office.json.

lamps.what: the anglepoise over the radio desk: its warm pool on the dockets, seen from the street at night (6 October, phase 1, item 1.1)

shops.sources: production/research/cab-office-interior-1990 (both notes: paper and voice radio, wood-effect tops, fabric swivel chairs on five-star bases, plastic trays, coiled cords, pot plants; the number signwritten on the glass); canon.md D19; his ruling of 3 October, 'Mickey's window shows its office'
shops.lumens_note: 4 October: the street runs on low light values (its sun at 3), so a room light is small in lumens: at 500 the room washed out (its dark wood counter cream, the night frame's median 190); 180 by day and 300 at night. The first read of black at 400 was the street's solid block behind the window (now hidden, hide_meshes).

shops.trade: pawnbroker (Rita's): watches, rings and chains in a glass counter, shelves crammed with radio cassettes, televisions, cameras, binoculars and clocks, boxes of stock, tools, a suitcase, every piece ticketed; a grille at night (not yet made)
shops.lit_note: Day 0.15, since the glass reflects (Thin Translucent): at 0.3 the street's reflection was a faint veil, at 0.08 the room read dim, at 0.03 the pane was nearly a mirror and the room a void (filmed 1 October; the research's 1/8 to 1/10 of the pavement is for an unlit shop, the Hook sheet's is lit and readable); night 0.7 glows without blowing the floor out; the night spill (a tube-white rect light in the window head, tipped 62 degrees down) at 350 lm on lighting channel 1 lights the display and lays a pool on the pavement and the road; the window bars are not on that channel, so they no longer flare (filmed at 250 to 2500 lm and from deep inside the shop, 1 October).

display.measured: the street model's own glass for this bay (street_glass_eg_bay2: panes at 5.245 to 5.265 m back, 0.70 to 2.91 m up, the door at 18.9 to 19.8 m) and its stallriser top (0.70 m)
